Bring your laptop with RStudio ready to use. **B1 is due at 1:30 p.m.**

Use the arrow keys to navigate the browser slides. The PDF is a printable,
offline copy.

Save the demonstration `.qmd` to your course folder and open it in RStudio.
Each numbered example is independently runnable: use its green arrow or
**Run Current Chunk**. The examples use base R. Rendering the document also
requires `knitr` and `rmarkdown`. The HTML preview displays evaluated output;
it does not run R in your browser. If using the optional project file, save
it beside the QMD and open the project first.

## During the seminar

We will map outcomes to numerical values, construct probability mass functions,
and compare exact calculations with simulated experiments. A voter-mobilization
example connects enumeration and counting to treatment counts.

We will use a polling model to study binomial counts and cumulative probabilities,
then examine transformations, expectation, variance, and independence. A waiting-time
example distinguishes failures before a first success from the total number of calls.

## After class

Rerun the demonstrations and change one input at a time. Explain the difference
between increasing the number of voters in a poll and increasing the number of
simulated polls. Practice translating each probability inequality into an R expression.

Assignment instructions and submission repositories are distributed separately
through the private-repository workflow.
